title: C4 262k capacity activation
outcome: coordinated four-rank transition, post-boot functional gates and full-context capacity proof passed; no promotion, no new baseline, performance not measured
coverage: One authorized coordinated four-rank transition to the C4 candidate, eight full-context capacity requests (four distinct request bodies submitted once cold and once on replay) and one single-request functional smoke. No native Rigmark suite was executed, so no throughput, latency, prefill or concurrency value is reported.
privacy: Numeric fields, safe protocol/settings fields and receipt digests only. Raw prompts, responses, cache salt, endpoint, host identities, private paths and generated payloads are omitted.

reference.relationship: The accepted E03 system identity with the SparkCache connector swapped to the C4 file, the KV pool cut from 16106127360 to 12884901888 bytes per rank and MAX_NUM_SEQS cut from 6 to 4. The request limit was unchanged at 262144 tokens. The frozen performance baseline is unchanged and was neither reproduced nor challenged.

configuration.sparkcache_connector_tracked_note: scripts/node/sparkcache/SHA256SUMS pins the E03 replay connector 5893f8747aa093874c46a0185f93c786265d99b5a4cd8da849a7471132422d66 and contains no entry for the C4 digest. The candidate overlay named in the private execution summary is not present in the current checkout.

lifecycle.end_state: healthy candidate left serving; base cluster.env unchanged at the E03 recipe; candidate overlay not persisted, so the next autostart recipe remained base E03
lifecycle.check_f0_identity_note: The identity check did not complete from the orchestrating workstation, which could not reach the service endpoint. The served recipe was confirmed from the per-rank launcher flags and the on-cluster live verification instead.

host_memory.modeled_copy_peak_note: Modeled, not measured. Sampled MemAvailable stayed above the 1.5 GiB per-rank floor throughout.

limitations: No native Rigmark suite was executed in this window, so no throughput, time-to-first-token, prefill or concurrency value is supported and this record cannot reproduce or challenge the frozen 2026-09-19 E03 performance reference.

The 625-block figure is a modeled capacity budget, not observed occupancy: zero samples show four requests running with at least 625 total blocks and the first qualifying sample is null. The highest common occupancy observed during the four-running replay interval was 581 blocks including the null block.
The cold phase never showed four simultaneous near-limit contexts; its peak was two running with two waiting.

Per-rank active residency is not independently measured and there is no one-to-one attribution from a verified restore to a specific request, so the four-context replay overlap rests on sixteen samples at four running plus four verified restores on every rank.
Connector counters such as store-skipped-busy and the per-group block decomposition are not exposed live.

Host memory minima are sampled observations at roughly half-second intervals, not bounds; rank 0 reached 4.934 GiB MemAvailable during the cold phase and 4.663 GiB during replay, and the approximately 3.3 GiB copy peak remains modeled.
The earlyoom journal window was empty on ranks 2 and 3, so the zero-intervention result on those ranks rests on the kernel journal alone.

The scripts/check-f0.py identity check did not complete from the orchestrating workstation because it could not reach the service endpoint; the served recipe was confirmed from the per-rank launcher flags and on-cluster live verification instead.

The C4 connector is not tracked in this repository and the candidate overlay named in the private execution summary is absent from the current checkout, so the recipe is reproducible only from the recorded launcher flags and the connector digest.
The phase elapsed seconds are wall-clock durations of a capacity probe, not benchmark measurements, and are not comparable with any frozen record.
